ledger.note: 1619: Buayan sinks under Maguindanao. The page: 'Buayan declines as Sultan Muhammad Kudarat of Maguindanao rises' (1619); by 1634 the Silongan-led confederacy disappears and Silongan is a petty king; in 1648 Rajah Baratamay ascends and Buayan comes 'under heavy Maguindanao influence' under Kudarat. Page silent on the word vassal or a boundary: the year and the pairing mirror the Maguindanao dossier's 1619-1671 span.

wars.name: Rajah Silongan against Maguindanao and Spain
wars.outcome: 'In April 1596, Rajah Silongan held off against the joint forces of Maguindanao and Spain.' In 1605 a peace treaty brokered by Melchor Hurtado recognises Silongan as paramount ruler of Maguindanao in exchange for his allegiance to Spain (8 September).
wars.note: Buayan raids reached Cebu, Negros, Panay, Batangas, Calamianes and Leyte in 1599-1603; on 22 July 1609 Silongan and Kapitan Laut Buisan wrote to the Spanish governor-general seeking forgiveness for their alliance with Ternate.

wars.name: Battle of the Malala River (American conquest)
wars.outcome: Datu Ali is killed at the Malala River on 22 October 1905 and Buayan is absorbed into the American colonial administration.
wars.note: Datu Piang betrayed Datu Uto in January 1899, took Bacat, later proclaimed himself 'Sultan of Mindanao' and cooperated with the Americans who landed in Cotabato in December 1899; Datu Ali was Uto's cousin and successor.
